en.title: Number of Processes and Total Power Within Each Processor's Range
en.description:
Each process has a power consumption power, and each processor can serve the processes in the closed interval [minPower,maxPower]. For each processor independently, output the number of processes in its range and the total power of those processes; this is not a one-time assignment of processes to different processors. Duplicate power values belong to different processes and are counted separately.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line contains n power values, followed by m lines of minPower maxPower. The original bounds are 1≤n≤12×10^5=1200000, 1≤m≤200000, 1≤power,minPower≤maxPower≤10^8 (power on its own is in 1..10^8). 1,200,000 is not misread as 120,000.
en.output: Output m lines in the input order of the processors, each containing the count and the total power.
en.explanation: The outputs are 4 31 / 2 13 / 3 21; 3 33 / 0 0; and 1 2 / 3 6. The text of the second original example wrongly says 2 processes; given its three-element array, it should be 3.
hints: Sort power and build packed unsigned 64-bit prefix sums. For each closed range, use lower_bound(min) and upper_bound(max) to get the indices [l,r); the count is r−l and the total is prefix[r]−prefix[l]. Release references to the power strings after reading, and do not keep multiple copies of nested results.
